ThingDef.label: fertilizer pack
ThingDef.description: Compacted, processed chicken manure, sealed into a transportable pack. Left on natural ground it slowly spoils and builds a layer of fertile soil over the land around it, reclaiming barren ground step by step: soft sand into sand, sand and bare cave stone into stony soil, stony soil into lichen-covered soil, lichen-covered soil into soil, and soil into ground crops grow best in. Unlike toxic wastepacks, fertilizer packs release no pollution and no poison gas; they are simply organic material doing what organic material does.\n\nA pack keeps as food keeps: warmth rots it in about ten days, cold holds it back, and freezing stops it outright. When the stack rots away each pack strikes about six cells. A cell takes one step along that progression only after three packs have struck it.
